findings.evidence: Finite.lean:70-83 vs Degree.lean:129-132. The proof body of `finiteDimensional_functionField` uses the extra instances only to derive `hfield`, which is precisely `degree_eq_finrank`'s own hypothesis (line 83: `φ.degree_eq_finrank hfield ▸ φ.degree_pos`); the residual mathematical content of the lemma is the one-line `of_finrank_pos` step. The transport step also duplicates the `IsFractionRing.ringHom_ext` argument already packaged as `fieldPullback_unique` (FunctionField.lean:191-198).
findings.fix: State it at the field level: `theorem finiteDimensional_functionField (φ : Isogeny W₁ W₂) [Algebra W₂.FunctionField W₁.FunctionField] (h : ∀ z, algebraMap W₂.FunctionField W₁.FunctionField z = φ.fieldPullback z) : FiniteDimensional W₂.FunctionField W₁.FunctionField := FiniteDimensional.of_finrank_pos (φ.degree_eq_finrank h ▸ φ.degree_pos)`. Factor the current `IsFractionRing.ringHom_ext` step out as its own lemma (`algebraMap W₂.FunctionField W₁.FunctionField = φ.fieldPullback` from the coordinate-level `h` and the tower) — it is independently useful for any consumer bridging coordinate-level to field-level data — and have `moduleFinite_intermediateRing` chain the two. Also correct the Design section (line 35-36), which asserts both results match `degree_eq_finrank`'s shape; as written the first does not.
findings.issue: `finiteDimensional_functionField` concludes `FiniteDimensional W₂.FunctionField W₁.FunctionField` but requires `[Algebra W₂.CoordinateRing W₁.FunctionField]`, `[IsScalarTower W₂.CoordinateRing W₂.FunctionField W₁.FunctionField]` and a coordinate-level `h` — none of which the conclusion mentions. The sibling it claims to match, `degree_eq_finrank` (Degree.lean:129), takes only `[Algebra W₂.FunctionField W₁.FunctionField]` and `h : ∀ z, algebraMap W₂.FunctionField W₁.FunctionField z = φ.fieldPullback z`. A consumer who did the natural thing — `letI := φ.fieldPullback.toRingHom.toAlgebra`, as `degree_comp` does at Degree.lean:163 — cannot use this lemma without manufacturing a coordinate-ring algebra structure and a tower instance it has no use for.

summary: Hypothesis strengths on the module-finiteness result are right (integrally-closed base, separability, parametrized algebra structures). But `finiteDimensional_functionField` is stated one level too low: a purely function-field conclusion carries two coordinate-ring instance arguments plus a coordinate-level `h`, so callers holding only the field-level structure cannot apply it.
